Subject: Short window of 5xxs + elevated tail latency — please advise

Hi Olga,

We observed an elevated error rate (mostly 502/503) and a clear 99th latency spike between 07:14 and 07:20 PST this morning affecting our ingestion pipeline. Our dashboards show a ~6 minute window where throughput dropped and retries spiked; our users saw timeouts for a subset of requests.

We opened a support ticket (BRIGHT-5123) but wanted to loop you directly because this intersects the SLA window in our contract. We believe the impact is larger than a routing blip and are requesting guidance on how Redwood will attribute this event for uptime calculations and whether an SLA credit applies.

Attached is a short snippet from our logs and a Grafana screenshot. Happy to share more traces if needed.

Attachments: [grafana_latencies_nov15.png (image/png), 360KB], [incident_snippet.log (text/plain)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Short window of 5xxs + elevated tail latency — please advise

Hi all,

Quick technical summary from our side after correlating Redwood traces with the log sample Adam provided:

- Timeline: 07:12:34–07:20:15 PST — bulk of client retries and elevated 99th latency. Peak at 07:15:02.
- Root cause signals: Our edge logs show a surge of 502 responses tied to a handful of external CDN POPs returning upstream connection errors between 07:14:50 and 07:16:30. Within Redwood's control plane, the serving runtime remained healthy; token processing and GPU queues did not spike concurrently.
- Impact scope: ~2.1% of BrightEdge requests in that interval experienced a failed path; an additional ~4% had >=1 retry/long tail latency before success.

Given the above, this looks like a partial degradation caused primarily by third-party CDN instability. Per our SLA appendix, we normally exclude third-party outages from uptime calculations if we can show the failure originated outside Redwood and if a customer’s traffic was routed through that third party. However — because BrightEdge saw retries/timeouts at the application level — I recommend we propose an apportionment rather than a full exclusion.

Proposed approach (draft):
- Window: 07:12:30–07:20:30 PST (conservative bounds)
- Affected unit: percentage of BrightEdge token requests that returned 5xx or exceeded 10s latency in that window (we measure ~6.1%).
- Credit calculation: apply proportional credit based on affected request percentage multiplied by the monthly uptime credit pool for the contract period. (I've sketched numbers in the attached spreadsheet.)

Attachments: [sla_credit_calc_v1.xlsx]

If BrightEdge prefers full exclusion, legal will need to confirm whether the CDN qualifies under the "third-party service" clause — we can provide the same evidence (edge logs, CDN incident reports).

Monica
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Adam Keller <adam.k@brightedge.com>

Subject: Re: Short window of 5xxs + elevated tail latency — please advise

Monica — thanks for the analysis. I appreciate the detail but our telemetry shows customer-facing errors beyond retried requests. We have internal dashboards that map requests to customer-facing failures and the incident caused an observable degradation in our SLIs (error budget burn for the day). From our perspective a third-party exclusion would not be appropriate: the failures propagated to the application tier and impacted our users.

We're asking Redwood to calculate the credit assuming this event counts against uptime. If you can share the exact numerator/denominator and the spreadsheet numbers you used, we can reconcile offline. For transparency I'm including a link to our traces: https://grafana.brightedge.com/d/abcd1234/high-latency-11-15

We reserve the right to escalate to procurement/legal if needed, but would prefer to resolve directly.

—Adam

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:47:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Short window of 5xxs + elevated tail latency — attribution proposal and next steps

Team — forwarding the thread to request formal sign-off on the proposed apportionment. Summary and ask:

Summary: Monica's telemetry ties the primary cause to a small set of CDN POP failures. Impact to BrightEdge traffic appears to be ~6.1% of requests in the conservative window. BrightEdge disputes the exclusion and wants the event counted against uptime.

Ask: Approve the apportionment-based credit proposal (spreadsheet attached) and provide any edits to wording for the customer communication. If legal or billing require a different treatment (full exclusion vs full credit), flag now — procurement has indicated BrightEdge may escalate.

Proposed customer-facing language (draft):
"We investigated the 2026-11-15 incident and found that a subset of BrightEdge requests were impacted by transient failures at a third-party CDN. Because the error path propagated to application-level retries and timeouts for some BrightEdge requests, Redwood proposes an apportionment-based credit equal to X% of the monthly uptime credit pool. Attached are the telemetry exports and the credit calculation for review. If BrightEdge disagrees with this approach, Redwood will escalate the matter to procurement/legal per the contract."

Please reply with Approve / Edit / Escalate by EOD Pacific.

Attachment: [sla_credit_calc_v1.xlsx]

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
